newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Police web nets French "Spiderman" on Sydney tower.
newsitem.headline: Police web nets French "Spiderman" on Sydney tower.

text.p: A French "Spiderman" who has climbed some of the world's tallest structures was caught in a police web on Thursday, half-way up Sydney's Centrepoint Tower.
Alain Robert, a 34-year-old rock climber from southern France, surprised police and security guards by crawling up the landmark tower's twisted outer cables soon after dawn.
But as a police helicopter circled overhead, Robert was nabbed by police as he passed a maintenance platform half-way up the 325-metre (1,066-foot) tower, Australia's tallest building.
Angry-looking police handcuffed Robert and took him away in a van. Officials said Robert was charged with illegally climbing up a building and was due to appear in court on Friday.

The Frenchman has scaled high buildings and structures around the world, including the Eiffel Tower in Paris, the Golden Gate Bridge in San Francisco and Hong Kong's Far East Finance Centre. He is regularly arrested and fined for his daredevil antics.
